selected_problem: Fresh canonical main enforced the write/delete operation set while staging, but apply trusted the persisted change.op after reload. Rewriting a staged operation to an unsupported value such as copy still followed the non-delete write path and mutated the workspace.
decision_basis: The repository already defines the legal changeset operation set as write/delete during stage, so revalidating the same set at apply is an existing protocol invariant rather than a new architecture choice.
Rollback is intentionally left able to recover already-APPLIED legacy artifacts rather than making a newly enforced staging rule destroy reversibility.
Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502; validation therefore used DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY（DWAC 源码契约重放） and exact local focused tests.

pre_fix_reality.focused_reproduction: EXPECTED_FAILURE: 1/2 PASS, 1/2 FAIL with Missing expected exception; a persisted op changed from write to copy was applied as a write.
pre_fix_reality.impact: A persisted STAGED artifact could escape the operation vocabulary that stage had already approved and still produce workspace side effects.

change: Apply preflight now rejects any persisted operation outside write/delete before preimage/postimage checks or workspace side effects.

validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed core/changesets.mjs content
validation.focused_tests: 4/4 PASS, 0 skipped across apply-preimage and apply-operation integrity
validation.supported_roundtrip: PASS: a normal persisted write still applies and rolls back exactly

truth_boundary: This restores the existing persisted operation vocabulary at the apply boundary. It is not an authenticated artifact mechanism and does not prevent a coherent rewrite that remains inside the legal write/delete protocol.
